# `lock-on` content schema

<!-- Generated by pnpm content:docs from the "lock-on" schema in src/content/registry.ts; do not edit. -->

One JSON file per entry in `src/content/data/lock-on/`. Fields marked "required" must be present;
every other field takes the default shown when omitted ("—" = stays absent).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | id | required | Profile id, e.g. "player". |
| `name` | string | required | Display name (debug tools and docs). |
| `notes` | string | required | Why these values (feel targets, references), for owner review. |
| `selectRange` | number > 0 ≤ 100 | required | Farthest a target can be picked or cycled to, m (eye to lock point). |
| `coneAngle` | number > 0 ≤ 180 | required | Pick and cycle only targets within this angle of the camera forward, degrees. |
| `breakRange` | number > 0 ≤ 100 | required | The lock breaks once the target is farther than this, m; ≥ selectRange. |
| `lostSightMs` | integer > 0 ≤ 10000 | required | The lock breaks once the target has been out of sight this long, ms; sight returning sooner keeps it. |
| `switchRange` | number > 0 ≤ 100 | required | When the locked target dies, the lock moves to the best other target this close, m, or releases. |
| `eyeHeight` | number > 0 ≤ 3 | required | Height above the player’s feet that sight lines and angles are measured from, m. |
| `minVisibility` | number > 0 ≤ 1 | required | A lock point is in sight when at least this much of its sight line is clear, 0–1. |
| `distanceWeight` | number 0–10 | required | Picking scores angle ÷ coneAngle + distanceWeight × distance ÷ selectRange (lowest wins); 0 ignores distance. |
| `priorityWeight` | number 0–10 | required | Each point of a target’s priority takes this much off its pick score. |
| `turnRate` | number > 0 ≤ 3600 | required | How fast the locked player turns to face the target, degrees/s. |
| `flick` | object | required | Cycling by flicking look input sideways while locked on: the right stick (the pad has no cycle button) or a fast mouse swipe. |
| `flick.stickThreshold` | number 0.1–1 | required | Right-stick sideways deflection that counts as a flick, 0.1–1. |
| `flick.stickRest` | number 0–0.9 | required | The stick must come back within this sideways deflection before the next flick, 0–0.9; below stickThreshold. |
| `flick.mouseCounts` | integer > 0 ≤ 10000 | required | Sideways mouse movement in one tick that counts as a flick, counts. |
| `flick.mouseRest` | integer 0–10000 | required | Sideways mouse movement in one tick at or below which the mouse is at rest, counts; below mouseCounts. |
| `framing` | object | required | Camera framing while locked (presentation only): keeps the player and target in view. |
| `framing.time` | number > 0 ≤ 2 | required | Seconds for the camera to swing about two thirds of the way to its lock-on framing (exponential ease), and back on release. |
| `framing.targetWeight` | number 0–1 | required | Where between the player’s head (0) and the target’s lock point (1) the camera aims. |
| `framing.pitchOffset` | number -45–45 | required | Added to the aim pitch, degrees; negative looks further down so the player stays in frame. |
